item.title: Inner Body Guided-Meditation (20 minutes) — Mon Aug 17, 6:30 PM
item.description:
The Mindful Stream (CA) "Awareness of the inner body takes you beyond the mind." - Eckhart Tolle
In this mediation session we will bring our attention here: to the inner body. Sessions are suitable for newcomers, those experienced in Tolle's teachings and anyone wishing to remain completely anonymous. They will last around 20 minutes and cameras and microphones will be disabled. (Depending on the situation, a free discussion may be held at the end with mics and cameras allowed.)

item.title: Awakening Awareness: Embracing This Moment — Tue Aug 18, 6:30 PM
item.description:
The Mindful Stream (CA) A session inspired by Eckhart Tolle's practices. Feel free to join as we get still and practise presence within this moment. We will discuss and observe the obstacles that, seemingly, block us from being present and bring awareness to our unconsciousness in a safe, inclusive and affirming way.
Sessions are suitable for newcomers, those experienced in Tolle's teaching and anyone wishing to remain completely anonymous.
See you there!
Please be aware that sessions will close if no members have joined after 10 minutes.
Emrys has been passionate about mindfulness since 2010 and since 2021 he has been organising free, weekly online meditation groups. For more information on his free Work of Byron Katie online mediation group, visit [this Meetup Group link](https://www.meetup.com/thework-runsfree/).
Source: Meetup: Mindful Petaluma

item.title: Simple Sitting Meditation — Wed Aug 19, 8:00 AM
item.description:
The Mindful Stream (CA) In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.
There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.
Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.
Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.
The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.
Source: Meetup: Mindful Petaluma

item.title: Wednesday Night Walk: Petaluma Downtown & Riverfront — Wed Sep 9, 6:00 PM
item.description:
"SONOMA COUNTY OUTDOORS" Wednesday Night Walk: Petaluma Downtown and Riverfront
* Want to walk for fitness and exercise? * New to walking and want to build up stamina? * Like a slower pace than our Tuesday Night Fitness Hike? * Would walking with a committed group of walkers help you?
If you said yes to any of these, then the Wednesday Night Walk in Petaluma is for you. We start at Aqus Cafe and take in the West Side of town, including some of Downtown, the Waterfront and a few of the Historic home of old Petaluma. We walk about 3-1/2 to 4-1/2 miles depending on weather conditions and the pace of the group that night.
Afterward if you have the time, join us at Aqus Cafe for a bite to eat and some liquid refreshment before heading home. Aqus Cafe is a true gem of a gathering place, restaurant, coffee house, and live music venue. But it's the people on either side of the counter that make this place so special.

item.title: Trans Magic! Exhibit Opening Party — Sat Aug 8, 2:00 PM — Petaluma Historical Library & Museum
item.description:
Saturday, August 8, 2:00 – 4:00 pm Petaluma Historical Library & Museum 20 4th Street (Corner of 4th & B Street) Exhibit Hours: Thursday – Sunday, 10 a.m. – 4 p.m. Sliding scale donations support our Exhibit!
Featuring Exhibit Tours, Music with DJ EM BASS, Community, Dancing! A community-curated exhibit celebrating the creativity, organizing, and history of trans and gender-expansive people in the North Bay and greater Bay Area. The exhibit traces a direct line from the gender-bending creativity of early 20th-century Vaudeville, to the radical resistance of the groundbreaking 1966 Compton’s Cafeteria Riot, and finally to the modern triumphs of community groups bringing joyful connection today.
Source: Petaluma Museum

item.title: Merging Music & Humanity — Sun Aug 9, 7:00 PM — Polly Klaas Community Theater
item.description: Turn your Sunday into a night to remember! Join us on August 9th at 7 PM for an unforgettable evening of music with one of New Orleans’ most distinctive pianists—Tom McDermott. Proceeds from this concert will directly help Global Healing’s ongoing efforts in Roatán, Honduras, continuing to support fire recovery and providing the assistance needed to facilitate the hospital’s services. In 2024, a shocking fire ravaged the sole public hospital on Roatán. Home to Global Healing’s pediatric clinic for over the past two decades, the hospital was vital for emergency care for both children and adults, performing urgent surgeries, and providing maternity services—like life-saving C-sections. Reduced to ashes, the hospital and clinic left Honduras with even fewer means to deliver essential medical care. All medical equipment was lost, and recovery is still ongoing. item.title: Furthest Waves Guitars Showcase — Fri Aug 28, 7:30 PM — The Phoenix Theater
item.description:
On Fri Aug. 28 Furthest Waves Guitars from Sonoma County will present an exciting guitar showcase at The Phoenix Theater in Petaluma from 8 pm to 11 pm.
The event is also a benefit for the Phoenix Teen Health program.
Come see, hear and feel these revolutionary lightweight nimble electric guitars and basses.
While this California built, smaller, light-weight, electric guitar was designed by a woman and originally designed with women, young people, and musicians of smaller stature in mind, we are finding this guitar is a lot of fun to play for everyone. It is a high quality, accessible and inclusive instrument for all.

item.title: Trans Magic: Owning Our Stories of Strength and Resilience — Thu Aug 6, 10:00 AM — Petaluma Historical Library & Museum
item.description:
August 6 – 30, 2026 Petaluma Historical Library & Museum 20 4th Street (Corner of 4th & B Street) Hours: Thursday – Sunday, 10 a.m. – 4 p.m. Admission Free, Donations Appreciated
A community-curated exhibit celebrating the creativity, organizing, and history of trans and gender-expansive people in the North Bay and greater Bay Area. The exhibit traces a direct line from the gender-bending creativity of early 20th-century Vaudeville, to the radical resistance of the groundbreaking 1966 Compton’s Cafeteria Riot, and finally to the modern triumphs of community groups bringing joyful connection today. item.title: Simple Sitting Meditation — Wed Aug 12, 8:00 AM
item.description:
The Mindful Stream (CA) In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.
There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.
Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.
Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.
The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.
